breakfast.name: Laxoox (Spongy Pancake)
ingredients: 2 cups flour (or mix of wheat and cornmeal)
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt with warm water to thin, pourable batter
Cover, ferment 2-4 hours or overnight — the batter should be bubbly and slightly sour
Heat a flat pan, pour batter in a spiral from outside to center
Cook on one side only — the top gets hundreds of tiny holes as steam escapes
The bottom should be golden, the top spongy and perforated
Roll or fold, serve with tea, honey, or stews
breakfast.description: Spongy, one-sided pancake covered in tiny holes — the fermented batter creates the characteristic perforations. Eaten at every meal in Djibouti, rolled around stews or dipped in honey.

breakfast.name: Foul Medames
instructions: Soak fava beans overnight, cook until very soft — 60 min or more
Mash roughly, leaving some beans whole for texture
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, add cumin and chili
Mix into beans
Add tomato, drizzle olive oil and lemon juice
Top with hard-boiled egg
Serve with laxoox for scooping
breakfast.description: Slow-cooked fava beans mashed with cumin, tomato, and olive oil — the same dish eaten across the Horn of Africa and Middle East, connecting Djibouti to both worlds.

breakfast.name: Muufo iyo Suqaar (Flatbread with Sautéed Meat)
ingredients: Muufo: corn flour, wheat flour, water, salt
Suqaar: 400g beef or goat (diced small), onion, green pepper, tomato, garlic, cumin, coriander, chili, oil, salt, lime
instructions: Make muufo: mix flours with water and salt, shape into thick disc, cook on flat griddle until firm and slightly charred on both sides
Make suqaar: heat oil, brown diced meat quickly
Add onion, pepper, garlic, cook until softened
Add tomato, cumin, coriander, chili
Cook until meat is tender and sauce coats the pieces
Squeeze lime over
Tear muufo into pieces, scoop up suqaar
breakfast.description: Thick corn flatbread with spiced sautéed meat — the muufo is dense and chewy, perfect for scooping up the saucy, spiced meat cubes. A hearty Djiboutian breakfast.

breakfast.name: Laxoox (Djibouti Sourdough Crepe)
ingredients: 2 cups flour (or mix of regular and whole wheat)
1 cup fermented batter (flour + water left overnight)
instructions: Mix fermented batter with flour, water, salt, touch of sugar — consistency of thin pancake batter
The fermentation gives it a tangy flavor and the signature bubbles
Pour onto hot, greased griddle or non-stick pan
Cook on one side only — do not flip
The surface develops hundreds of tiny holes as steam escapes from the fermented batter
The bottom is golden, the top is spongy and crater-covered
Stack and serve with butter and honey drizzled on top
Eat by tearing and dipping — this is breakfast from the Horn of Africa to the Gulf
breakfast.description: Djibouti's spongy, crater-covered breakfast crepe — fermented batter poured on a hot griddle, cooked on one side only. The hundreds of tiny holes form naturally as the fermentation creates steam. Laxoox (also called canjeero) is viral for its hypnotic bubble-forming process on the griddle.

lunch.name: Skoudehkaris (Spiced Lamb Rice)
instructions: Brown lamb with onions and garlic
Add spices and tomatoes
Add rice and water
Cook covered until rice absorbs liquid
lunch.description: Djibouti's national dish — fragrant lamb and rice.

lunch.name: Maraq (Spiced Soup)
instructions: Simmer meat until tender
Add diced vegetables
Season with spices
Cook until vegetables are soft
Garnish with cilantro
lunch.description: Warming spiced meat and vegetable soup.

lunch.name: Cambulo (Red Bean and Rice)
instructions: Cook rice normally
Mix hot rice with cooked beans
Add generous butter or ghee
Drizzle sesame oil
Sweeten with sugar — yes, it's sweet, savory, and oily at the same time
Serve as a main dish
lunch.description: Sweet-savory red bean rice — the butter, sesame oil, and sugar combination seems unusual but is beloved in Djibouti. Eaten during Ramadan and celebrations.

dinner.name: Fah-Fah (Goat Soup)
instructions: Boil goat meat with onions 45 min
Add tomatoes, chili, spices
Simmer 15 more min
Garnish with cilantro
Serve with canjeero
dinner.description: Hearty goat soup — Djibouti's comfort food.

dinner.name: Sambuusa (Stuffed Pastries)
ingredients: Pastry: 2 cups flour, oil, water, salt
Filling: 300g ground beef or lamb, onion (finely diced), garlic, chili flakes, cumin, coriander, salt
instructions: Make thin pastry: mix flour, oil, water, salt, knead until smooth
Roll very thin, cut into strips
Make filling: cook ground meat with onion, garlic, spices until dry
Place filling on strip, fold into triangle shape, sealing as you go
Each fold creates a neat triangular pocket
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve hot with lime — they're best eaten immediately
dinner.description: Crispy fried triangular pastries filled with spiced meat — the Djiboutian version of samosa. Every household has their own spice blend. Essential during Ramadan iftar.

dinner.name: Bariis Iskukaris (Spiced Rice with Meat)
ingredients: Xawaash spice mix: cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper
instructions: Brown meat in oil with one sliced onion
Add garlic, tomatoes, xawaash spice mix
Add water, simmer 25 min until meat is tender
Fry second onion until golden
Add raisins, carrot, potato to the meat
Layer soaked rice on top
Add enough broth to cover rice by 1cm
Cook covered on low 20 min until rice absorbs all liquid
The rice should be fluffy and each grain separate, perfumed with the spice mix
Serve on a large communal platter, meat underneath rice
dinner.description: Djibouti's celebration rice — spiced with xawaash (the Somali-Djiboutian spice blend), layered over slow-cooked lamb. Served on a communal platter, eaten together.

snacks.name: Bajiya (Lentil Fritters)
instructions: Grind lentils coarsely
Mix with onion, chili, cumin
Fry spoonfuls until golden

snacks.name: Nafaqo (Stuffed Potato Balls)
ingredients: Filling: 200g ground beef, onion, garlic, cumin, chili, salt
instructions: Mash potatoes smooth
Cook filling: brown meat with onion, garlic, spices until dry
Take a ball of potato, flatten in palm, place filling in center
Close potato around filling, shaping into smooth ball
Dip in beaten egg, roll in breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden all over
Cut open to reveal the surprise meat center
snacks.description: Crispy breaded potato balls with a spiced meat center — popular street food, especially during Ramadan evenings.

desserts.name: Halwo (Cornstarch Halva)
instructions: Dissolve cornstarch in water
Make sugar syrup
Cook cornstarch mixture, add butter and sugar syrup
Stir until thick and translucent
Add spices, set in mold

desserts.name: Bur Muusbaar (Date Balls)
instructions: Mash dates with a little ghee until sticky
Mix in ground peanuts and cardamom
Shape into small balls
Roll in toasted sesame seeds
Let firm up at room temperature
desserts.description: Date balls rolled in sesame — a sweet snack that stores well in the heat. Dates are central to Djiboutian food culture, especially during Ramadan.

drinks.name: Shaah (Spiced Tea)
instructions: Boil tea with spices 5 min
Add milk and sugar
Strain and serve hot

drinks.name: Qishr (Coffee Husk Tea)
instructions: Boil coffee husks with spices 10 min
Strain, sweeten
Serve hot
drinks.description: Tea brewed from coffee cherry husks.
